AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#634 @ dbc10b7b68436dad567e87057d240fbc5f51a4a8 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Independent T4 first audit, paired with mobile #325 `b0c02156dd86f00e0bfef80a7b517c46ddfb8f2d`; **A/B/C: 0/4/1**. No prior AUDIT comment existed at the initial read; these are independent findings, not builder self-attestation. [Backend candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634), [mobile contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/325).

### Must fix

**B-634-1 — A stale approval can approve a different, newly moved request and confirm the old time.** `src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:280-306,753-763` loads the requested interval but compare-and-set checks only `{id,status}`; client reschedule `:377-432` can change requested → requested without changing that status. Deterministic probe: pause approval immediately before its scheduled update, move the request 10:00 → 11:00, then release approval; approval fulfills instead of returning SESSION_STATE_CHANGED, and its confirmation still uses `existing.start_at` (10:00). The exclusion constraint does not fence the reviewed booking revision. Minimal fix: fence transitions against the actual interval/revision read (and validate time in the fenced transaction); build notifications from the committed revision, not stale input. Cover approve/decline/complete/cancel versus same-status moves, including moves across the start boundary, without cutting rescheduling. [Reviewed lifecycle](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

**B-634-2 — A transient failure permanently consumes a reminder, while metrics report it dispatched.** `src/scheduling/jobs/reminder.job.ts:185-197,217-226` inserts the unique delivery claim before attempting delivery, ignores the emitter's returned outcome, and never retries/releases a failed claim; `src/notifications/emitters/booking.emitter.ts:391-438` intentionally catches both channel failures and returns `{inapp:'failed',push:'failed'}`. Probe: both in-app writes and pushes fail on the first 1h sweep, recover before the next sweep; zero delivered rows/pushes remain and both recipients are skipped forever. A crash after claiming has the same loss window; claimDelivery also treats every database error as a duplicate. Minimal fix: durable recoverable delivery state/lease/outbox keyed by session revision and recipient/kind, channel-aware success and retry semantics, distinguishing P2002 from real database failures. Preserve preference suppression and concurrent-replica idempotency; prove recovered delivery, partial-channel failure, interrupted claims and reschedule/cancel fencing. This is the acknowledged launch delivery-recovery prerequisite, not a request to disable launch reminders. [Reminder/emitter seam](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

**B-634-3 — Finishing provisioning overwrites a newer coach-entered link.** `src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:852-859,884-942` snapshots the row, awaits providers/audit, then updates solely by session ID; the concurrent manual-link update is not fenced. Probe with the actual stub adapters: pause calendar creation, save `https://meet.example.com/new-room` successfully through attachManualVideoLink, release provisioning; the final saved link becomes null. Thus a successful coach action and link-ready notification can be invalidated even while Google/Zoom remain off. Cancellation/rescheduling while provisioning is in flight is likewise not checked at commit. Minimal fix: reserve/fence provisioning against the current session revision/status and link state, preserve newer manual edits, avoid sending obsolete confirmations, and clean up any real artifacts created for a superseded revision. Test manual-link, cancel and move interleavings with delayed adapters. [Provisioning seam](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

**B-634-4 — Past-session pagination loses rows sharing the boundary timestamp.** `src/scheduling/scheduling.service.ts:475-483` orders by `(start_at DESC,id DESC)` but the next-page predicate is only `start_at < before`; mobile `src/hooks/useCalendar.ts:127-133` passes the last start_at alone. Canceled/declined rows can legitimately share one time, and a client may have different coaches at the same instant. Probe: 21 canceled past rows at one timestamp, page size 20; first page has 20, next has zero instead of one. Minimal fix: an opaque or compound `(start_at,id)` cursor with the matching lexicographic predicate, update mobile #325, and test ties spanning pages without duplicates or omission. [Backend paging](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634), [mobile cursor](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/325).

### Optional

**C-634-1 — Keep rollback ownership of the shared extension explicit.** `prisma/migrations/20270222000000_scheduling_lifecycle_integrity/down.sql:8-17` says btree_gist is dropped last but actually drops it second, unconditionally, even if forward reused a pre-existing extension. RESTRICT safely refuses when another catalog object depends on it, but the documented down sequence then cannot finish as written on that database. Prefer leaving the shared extension installed or remove it only with attributable ownership and an explicit preflight/runbook; do not tell the operator to drop unrelated dependencies. CI's empty-schema down/up is not a populated-production extension-ownership proof. [Migration scope](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

### Evidence and boundaries

Reviewed lifecycle/access/view/open-slot computation, controller/DTO/module and schema/migration contracts, reminder/emitter and mobile API/routing/time/calendar/coach surfaces and their acceptance tests. The only CI edit adds the actual live scheduling suite to the required MWB invocation; no gate is weakened. The main merge has one prod-switch conflict: independently reconstructed tree `6ac629a28ae3c2262b8a1d3019d44b15126bae3d` equals integration `9a1f44bb` everywhere except the two explicitly reviewed metadata files (prod-switches.yml and src/common/env-validation.ts); excluding those files, remaining own zero-context patch IDs both equal `752ec0827b4ce73ed593148aeb33f2a205e2b527`. The resolution preserves #624 registration/inventory and records truthful explicit-on semantics; final dbc10b7b only adds actionable open-slot error text and its test. [Candidate and integration history](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

Local exact-head commands, via heavy.sh: private Prisma generation PASS; `env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath test/scheduling-lifecycle-integrity.spec.ts test/scheduling-reminder-delivery.spec.ts test/booking-emitter.spec.ts test/slot-computer-bookable.spec.ts test/scheduling.service.spec.ts` **5 suites / 100 tests PASS**, exit 0. Auditor-only `test/audit-sol111-scheduling-probe.spec.ts -t AUD-SOL` **4 independent assertions FAIL as expected**, 48 existing tests filtered out, exit 1; this reuses the candidate fake and production service/adapters/emitter with only deterministic delay/failure fixtures, not changed production code or a claimed live database run. Probe and logs are preserved in `ops/evidence/AUD-SOL-111/634-independent-probe*`. [Audited candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634).

All ten required checks plus forward/reversibility SUCCESS at this head; actual build reports **644 suites / 11,067 passing tests**, 20 suites / 209 tests skipped and five todo. Required MWB executes the live scheduling suite, including PostgreSQL overlap floor/preflight and advisory-lock waits: seven suites / 60 tests pass overall; existing RLS live checks also pass. These cover different interleavings from the four failing independent probes and do not close them. [Build execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/36975417075/job/110738072186), [live concurrency execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/36975417075/job/110738071955), [schema parity](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/36975417088/job/110738072344).

No push, merge, workflow dispatch, live/local PostgreSQL or production action. Retain operator-owned populated overlap/extension preflight and coordinated #632/#634/mobile rollout, explicit BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED=on, and iOS/Android delivery/tap/calendar-editor acceptance; green CI is not launch acceptance. [Declared rollout prerequisites](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/634), [device prerequisites](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/325).

AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#634 @ dbc10b7b68436dad567e87057d240fbc5f51a4a8 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Independent T4 first audit (S-SCHED-2 booking lifecycle, migration `20270222000000_scheduling_lifecycle_integrity`), paired with mobile #325 @ `b0c02156dd86f00e0bfef80a7b517c46ddfb8f2d`. **My count: A0 / B4 / C5.** Sol's verdict (comment 5955780870) landed while I was auditing. I reproduced the overlapping findings myself and cite Sol's IDs rather than adding duplicates. My new findings continue the numbering.

### B (must fix)

**B-634-1 (concur with Sol): approve, decline and cancel are not fenced against a same-status time move.** I reproduced this independently.
- Evidence: `src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:758-761`. `compareAndSet` filters `{ id, status }` only. A client reschedule keeps `requested` while changing the time (`:416-432`), and reschedule's own CAS already fences `start_at` (`:422`).
- Probe (`test/audit-probe-634.spec.ts`, fake DB + real services): I held approve's CAS, moved the request from Tue 10:00 to 11:00 PDT, then released approve.
  - The row ended `scheduled` at `2026-10-06T18:00Z` (11:00).
  - The client's push said "Coach Kim confirmed your Quick Q/A Call on Tue, Oct 6, 10:00 AM PDT." It came from `existing.start_at` at `:301-307`.
- Minimal fix:
  - Add `start_at` and `end_at` from `existing` to the CAS `where` clause, so a moved row returns 409 `SESSION_STATE_CHANGED`.
  - Build the notification from the updated row.
  - Optionally accept `expected_start_at` from the inbox for stale cards.
  - Add a test for the interleaving above.

**B-634-2 (concur with Sol): a failed reminder delivery consumes the claim and still counts as dispatched.**
- Evidence: `src/scheduling/jobs/reminder.job.ts:185-197` claims first, then calls `emit`. `booking.emitter.ts` now returns a failure outcome instead of throwing, and the job ignores it (`dispatched += 1`). `claimDelivery` at `:217-227` treats every error as a duplicate.
- The claim-first pattern was already on main (`reminder.job.ts:144-182`). It matters now because reminders are ON at launch (OR-110-5).
- Minimal fix:
  - Check the returned outcome.
  - On failure of both channels, delete the claim so the next sweep retries.
  - Count `dispatched` only on real delivery.
  - Return false only for P2002.

**B-634-4 (concur with Sol): the past-sessions cursor drops rows that share the boundary `start_at`.** I reproduced this independently.
- Evidence: `src/scheduling/scheduling.service.ts:480-482` orders by `(start_at desc, id desc)` but pages with `start_at < before` only.
- Probe: one client had two past rows at the same 10:00 (declined, then rebooked and completed) plus one earlier row. Paging with `limit 1` returned `["tie-a","early"]`, while the full list was `["tie-a","tie-b","early"]`.
- Minimal fix: use a compound `(before, before_id)` cursor with the predicate `start_at < b OR (start_at = b AND id < bid)`. Mobile `useCalendar.ts:127-133` must send the id. Add a test where a tie spans pages.

**B-634-5 (new): restoring an archived former welcome type fails every time with a false "landed at the same time" 409.**
- Archiving leaves `is_welcome=true`. After the coach marks another type as welcome, the mobile Restore action (`CoachAppointmentTypesScreen.tsx:140-147`) sends only `{ archived: false }`.
- In `updateSessionType` (`scheduling.service.ts:293-303`), `markWelcome` is only true when `dto.is_welcome === true`. So the other active welcome is not cleared, and the update violates `SessionType_one_active_welcome_per_coach` (`migration.sql:29-31`, `WHERE is_welcome AND archived_at IS NULL`).
- `writeWelcomeAware` at `:543-548` then maps P2002 to `SESSION_STATE_CHANGED`: "Another change to your welcome call type landed at the same time". That is not true, and every retry fails. A natural flow hits this: archive the day-1 welcome, create a new welcome, then restore the old type.
- No test covers restoring a welcome type.
- Minimal fix: when restoring a row with `existing.is_welcome` while `dto.is_welcome` is undefined and another active welcome exists, set `data.is_welcome = false` (keep the current welcome). Add a test against the real index in the live spec.

### C (follow-up)

- **C-634-1 (concur with Sol):** `down.sql:13-14` drops `btree_gist` unconditionally, even when the forward migration reused an extension that already existed. Leave the extension in place, or drop it only if this migration created it.
- **B-634-3 (Sol): an unfenced provisioning update can overwrite a manual link. I grade this C.**
  - The final `coachingSession.update({ where: { id } })` at `:932-942` was already on main (`:649`).
  - Provisioning runs inline before approve and book return, with stub and manual adapters only, so the race needs a second device inside a sub-second window.
  - Fencing on `video_url` / `status` is still the right fix.
- **C-634-2:** the preflight (`migration.sql:56-73`) does not count active rows with `end_at < start_at`. `tsrange(start_at, end_at)` (`:77-80`) then aborts the deploy with a raw range error. Add a second count that RAISEs with an actionable message.
- **C-634-3 (pair):** the upcoming scope (`scheduling.service.ts:486-490`) has no cursor and no status filter, and is capped at 100. The mobile inbox and agenda filter the first 100 rows on the device, and those rows include cancelled and declined sessions. A busy coach can therefore miss a pending request, which still holds its slot. Add `status=` or exclude terminal statuses, and add a cursor.
- **C-634-4 (product):** when a client moves a confirmed approval-type session (`:416-419`), the confirmed time is released at once. If the coach declines, the client has nothing, and the decline push does not say the original time is gone. Either keep the original until the new time is approved, or disclose it (see the mobile C on #325).

### Evidence
- Head re-read: `dbc10b7b` throughout.
- All 10 required checks are SUCCESS at this head (build-and-test, rls-floor-guard, rls-live-tests, mwb-3-live-tests, npm audit, CodeQL JS/TS, Banned cast tokens, build-sbom, danger, Schema parity). Forward and reversible migrations are also SUCCESS. Shellcheck fails as before (SC2015, ignored).
- Merge-tree with main `e5d10bd8` (#604) is clean (tree `f0ef58d3`). Main's delta and the PR share only `prod-switches.yml` and `src/common/env-validation.ts`, in disjoint hunks.
  - The seam is good: #604 throttler rows plus #634 `BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED` explicit-on copy.
  - The PR adds no `@Throttle` decorators. Its only new env read is `BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED === 'on'`, which is ON at launch under OR-110-5 and is not a finding.
- Locally at this head via heavy.sh: `env CI=false npx jest --runInBand --forceExit` passed 9 suites / 139 tests (lifecycle-integrity, booking-emitter, reminder-delivery, slot-computer-bookable, scheduling.service, booking-reminder.job, permissions, overrides, plus my 2-test probe).
- Checked and not a finding:
  - "participant-only" means the lead coach and client. No scheduling code writes SessionParticipant.
  - Reschedule not moving provider artifacts matches main.
  - `pending_provider` is never written now.
- No push, merge, dispatch or production action.

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#634 @ 2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

T4 paired scheduling re-audit. **A/B/C = 0/1/0.** B-634-1/3/4/5 and C-634-1/2/3 close; the approval-type move warning is accepted under the operator ruling, not a finding. B-634-2 is only partially closed: the lease/receipt implementation works inside the selection window, but a real next cron tick cannot recover all of its retry rows. [Lifecycle and cursor changes](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/src%2Fscheduling%2Fscheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts), [list/restore changes](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/src%2Fscheduling%2Fscheduling.service.ts), [migration](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/prisma%2Fmigrations%2F20270222000000_scheduling_lifecycle_integrity%2Fmigration.sql).

### B-634-2 — recoverable reminders disappear when the next cron tick leaves the due band

`src/scheduling/jobs/reminder.job.ts:155-157,181-183,215-222` selects sessions only in `[now+55m, now+65m]` / `[now+23h45m, now+24h15m]`; the retry/expired-lease lookup is reached only for those selected sessions, rather than selecting recoverable delivery-log work independently. [Actual cron and query](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/src%2Fscheduling%2Fjobs%2Freminder.job.ts).

Independent exact-service counterexample: at the final 1h-window tick a session starts in 55 minutes and both recipients fail delivery, leaving two retry rows at attempt 1; advance the fake clock by the real five-minute cron interval, recover transport, and run again: the session is still upcoming at +50m, but zero rows are selected, zero deliveries occur, and both retry rows remain stranded indefinitely. The same window-boundary defect applies to 24h recovery and an expired claim at the final tick; the added nominal recovery cases rerun at the same clock, so do not establish next-tick recovery. [Candidate recovery harness](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/test%2Fscheduling-lifecycle-integrity.spec.ts), [actual selection](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/src%2Fscheduling%2Fjobs%2Freminder.job.ts).

Minimal fix: separately select bounded retry/expired-lease work for still-upcoming sessions, verify current session status/revision and recipient before delivery, preserve settled-channel receipts, and explicitly retire stale/canceled/exhausted work; add advancing-clock tests at both final window boundaries and for a worker crash, rather than only immediate same-clock reruns. [Recovery implementation to extend](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/2a07ab25ef0b4b1c563d7c8542fb3abc6018cf0c/src%2Fscheduling%2Fjobs%2Freminder.job.ts).
